name: The Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order
dates: Thirteenth century · Florence and Monte Senario
history: Seven men of Florence, members of a confraternity devoted to Our Lady, who left their homes and businesses in 1233 to live together in poverty and prayer. They withdrew to Monte Senario outside the city and founded the Order of the Servants of Mary, the Servites, known for their devotion to the Seven Sorrows of Our Lady. They were canonised together in 1888.
life: Thirteenth-century Florence was rich, busy and torn by faction. The seven, most of them merchants and some married or widowed, met in a lay confraternity devoted to the Virgin. Servite tradition holds that on the feast of the Assumption in 1233 Our Lady inspired them to leave the world. Having provided for their families, they lived together in a poor house outside the walls, then moved to the solitude of Monte Senario, where they lived in great austerity. People came to them for guidance, and they began to accept disciples. Adopting the Rule of Saint Augustine, they became an order of friars, preaching and serving in the towns, and received the final approval of the Holy See in 1304. In religion they were named Bonfilius, Alexis, Manettus, Amideus, Hugh, Sostenes and Buonagiunta. Alexis Falconieri, the last of them, lived to a great age and died on this day in 1310.
prayerTo: Holy Founders, you left the riches of Florence to stand with Mary beneath the cross of her Son. Pray for all who serve her, for the Servite friars and sisters, and for me, that I may share her sorrows with love, leave behind whatever keeps me from God, and find true brotherhood in Christ. Amen.
penance: Pray the Rosary of the Seven Sorrows, or simply one Hail Mary for each of Our Lady’s sorrows. Give up one comfort today as an offering to her.
meditation: Seven busy men left their counting houses to stand with Mary at the foot of the cross. What would you need to leave to stand there with her?
